title: rhinanthus asperulus var. rohlenae
intro: Rhinanthus asperulus var. rohlenae, commonly known as the alpine serpour, is a flowering plant species within the family Orobanchaceae. This plant is a parasitic species, meaning it obtains its nutrients by connecting to the roots of other plants, typically grasses. The alpine serpour is reported to have various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may contribute to its potential in treating conditions such as arthritis and cancer. The bioactive constituents of Rhinanthus asperulus var. rohlenae include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to be responsible for its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects.
